findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at import time, not per instance
findings.body: The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` created via `from_integration` (which never passes `queued`) gets the process-start timestamp instead of the time the change was actually queued. The field should be declared with `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Any future logic that relies on `queued` (e.g. expiring stale assignment sources to break long-running sync cycles, or logging latency) will be silently wrong, and the new test `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, which masks the defect. Additionally, embedding a `datetime` in `assignment_source_dict` (via `to_dict()` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound.apply_async` kwargs) makes the task kwargs non-JSON-serializable; if the deployment's Celery task serializer is JSON, `apply_async` will raise, breaking all outbound assignee sync. Since `queued` is never consumed, either drop it or serialize it explicitly.

findings.title: from_dict performs no type validation, so malformed data silently disables cycle protection
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` only catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` from the constructor, but the dataclass constructor performs no type checking. A dict like `{"source_name": "x", "integration_id": "123"}` (string id) or one where `queued` is a string (which is exactly what a JSON round-trip of `to_dict()` produces, since `datetime` serializes to a string) is accepted without error and yields an `AssignmentSource` whose `integration_id` is a `str`. In `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`, `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` then compares `str` to `int`, always evaluates False, and the same-integration outbound sync is NOT suppressed — reintroducing the sync loop this PR is meant to fix, with no error or log. `from_dict` should validate/coerce the types (or at minimum compare with `int(sync_source.integration_id)` at the check site).

findings.title: Abstract sync_assignee_outbound signature not updated for the new assignment_source kwarg
findings.body: The task `sync_assignee_outbound` now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, and the abstract method `sync_status_outbound` in the same class was explicitly updated to declare `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`. However, the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` (line 397) was NOT updated — it only tolerates the new kwarg through `**kwargs: Any`. Any provider implementation that shadows this method without `**kwargs` (or without an `assignment_source` parameter) will raise `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source'` at runtime inside the Celery task; because `TypeError` is not in the task's retry exclude list, it will be retried 5 times before failing, generating noise and never syncing. The abstract signature should declare the parameter explicitly so implementers are forced to accept it.

findings.title: No test covers the actual inbound-webhook suppression path or cross-integration propagation
findings.body: The only suppression test (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`) constructs the `AssignmentSource` by hand and passes it directly to `GroupAssignee.objects.assign`, bypassing the real webhook plumbing. The end-to-end path the PR claims to fix — `sync_group_assignee_inbound` building the source from the integration, passing it through `GroupAssignee.objects.assign`, through `sync_group_assignee_outbound.apply_async` (including the dict serialization/deserialization via `AssignmentSource.to_dict`/`from_dict`), and finally the `should_sync` suppression in the task — is never exercised. This is exactly where the `from_dict` type/serialization defects would surface. Additionally, there is no test that a *different* integration's external issue still receives the outbound sync when an `assignment_source` is present (the "should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward" behavior), so a regression that over-blocks propagation would go undetected.
